display.purpose: The h1 name on the home hero and sub-page section headers.

title.purpose: Card titles, service titles, and the brand mark — the highest-emphasis line inside a component.

body.purpose: Default paragraph copy; a compact 13.5px variant is used for card/service descriptions.

label.purpose: Section titles, nav links, the terminal prompt, footnote, and status-tag pills.

shadows.name: card-hover-lift
shadows.purpose: The only shadow in the system; applied to cards/service tiles on hover alongside a -5px lift.

motion.name: hover-standard
motion.purpose: Default transition speed for button/card hover, nav underline, and color transitions.

motion.name: reveal-on-scroll
motion.purpose: Fade+translateY(18px→0) entrance for content blocks as they enter the viewport, staggered up to 240ms.

motion.name: typewriter
motion.purpose: Hero prompt and name type themselves in on page load.

motion.name: cursor-blink
motion.purpose: Blinking block cursor after the hero h1.

components.name: Primary Button

components.name: Ghost Button

components.name: Card
components.description: Service tile or project card — flat at rest, lifts with a soft mint-tinted shadow on hover.
components.html:
Website Development

Design and development of websites, including multilingual sites.

components.description: Project status badge (live / shipped / completed / design).
components.css: .ds-tag-pill { font-family: 'SFMono-Regular', Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', Menlo, Courier, monospace; color: #d4a72c; font-size: 11px; border: 1px solid #3a3120; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 10px; white-space: nowrap; }

components.name: Navigation Link
components.description: Top nav link with a left-growing underline on hover/active.
components.css: .ds-nav-link { font-family: 'SFMono-Regular', Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', Menlo, Courier, monospace; color: #8b949e; font-size: 13px; position: relative; text-decoration: none; padding-bottom: 2px; transition: color .15s ease; } .ds-nav-link::after { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 0; right: 100%; bottom: -3px; height: 1px; background: #4fd1a5; transition: right .2s ease; } .ds-nav-link:hover, .ds-nav-link--active { color: #4fd1a5; } .ds-nav-link:hover::after, .ds-nav-link--active::after { right: 0; }

narrative.overview: The site reads as a single terminal session left running late at night: a whoami prompt, // comments, a blinking text cursor, monospace type throughout. It is precise and quietly confident — the craft is meant to speak for itself rather than announce itself, so there is no marketing chrome, no gradient hero illustration, no glassmorphism. Yet it is not cold: the near-black background is offset by a warm amber secondary and two slow-drifting blurred color blobs that give the dark canvas ambient glow, like monitor bloom in a dark room, rather than stark cyberpunk starkness. Everything, including headings, is set in the same monospace stack. Hierarchy comes from size, weight, and color, not from switching typefaces — this is deliberate and load-bearing, not an oversight to "fix" with a display font.
keyCharacteristics: One font family for the entire system; hierarchy is size/weight/color only.
Flat surfaces at rest; depth and glow appear only on hover/interaction.
A single accent (mint) carries all interactive/primary meaning; amber is reserved for status-like content (role title, project tags).
Ambient, not decorative: background blobs and the scanline overlay create atmosphere without competing with content.
Motion is purposeful and fully disabled under prefers-reduced-motion (typewriter, cursor blink, blob drift, reveal-on-scroll, hover lifts).

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Terminal Mint is the only color that means "interactive." Signal Amber marks status/metadata and must never double as a link, button, or active-state color — mixing the two collapses the system's only semantic distinction.

rules.name: The One Font Rule
rules.body: No second typeface is ever introduced for "elegance" or contrast. If a new element needs more visual weight, it gets a larger size or Bright White, not a different font.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow at rest. Shadow is exclusively a hover/interaction signal, never a static styling choice — a component that needs to look "important" gets a border or Bright White text, not a permanent shadow.

dos: Do keep the entire system on one monospace font family; introduce new hierarchy through size, weight, or the three neutral text colors.
Do keep cards and panels flat at rest and reserve shadow for the hover-lift state only.
Do use Signal Amber strictly for status/metadata (role line, project tags) and never for links, buttons, or other interactive elements.

Do respect prefers-reduced-motion on every animation (typewriter, cursor blink, blob drift, reveal-on-scroll, hover transforms) — this is already implemented site-wide and must be preserved in any new component.
Do keep the content column narrow (820px max-width) — this is a reading-width personal site, not a wide marketing layout.
donts: Don't introduce a second (serif/display) typeface for "polish" — it breaks the terminal illusion the whole system is built on.
Don't add gradients, glassmorphism, or drop shadows at rest — the only permitted shadow is the single hover-lift value documented in Elevation & Depth.
Don't use rounded/pill shapes beyond the documented radii (4px/6px/10px/50%) or introduce heavier, more playful corner rounding.
Don't invent additional accent colors — Terminal Mint and Signal Amber are the only two, each with a fixed, non-overlapping role.
